additional_info.subject: RE: ID0481199-DC/Si-D/NL- [Y2 / S9 313873507001] Van Den Haak-data from AC MID meter CRM:00315003129
additional_info.body:
Dear Kanika, Dear Friso,
I am reaching out from the Technical Support Team in regards of ticket
ID0481199.
This ticket was handed over to me and I already aligned with my Catalina on the previous history and discussion around the topic. As I understand, the ticket was opened to have the AC Income meter values in the OCPP MeterValues messages, and I understand that your request would be to see the 3-Phases AC values in the mesages.
Unfortunately, some incorrect information have been conveyed to you so far, as it is not possible to see 3-Phase AC values in the OCPP MeterValues messages.
The measurands “Current.Import”, “Voltage”, and “Energy.Active.Import.Register” are sent split per each phase only in case of AC charging, and not for DC charging, regardless the presence of AC Income Meter.
Since charger
Y2/S9 313873507001
has not AC socket, it will not be possible to see such values split among 3-Phases. Unfortunately, this information was communicated incorrectly, as the example brought to you was referring to an OCPP MeterValues message related to a AC Charging.
Based on OCPP 1.6J Protocol, the “Energy.Active.Import.Register” represents the numerical value read from the "active electrical energy" (Wh or kWh) register of the (most authoritative) electrical meter measuring energy imported (from the grid supply)".
For example, with a MeterValues.req with specified connector Id, the charger will send the meter value at the outlet:
2026-04-10T13:00:00.093385+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/23863087fc2f[823]: OCPP: Send command: MeterValues (3c7e5bf2-983e-4404-94f3-4b6e8ab62c3f) - {"connectorId":1,"meterValue":[{"timestamp":"2026-04-10T13:00:00.091Z","sampledValue":[{"value":"24454686","location":"Outlet","unit":"Wh","measurand":"Energy.Active.Import.Register","context":"Sample.Clock"}]}]}
In case instead of a MeterValues.req with connector Id=0 (whole charger), the charger will send the meter value at the inlet:
2026-04-10T13:00:00.023489+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/23863087fc2f[823]: OCPP: Send command: MeterValues (c04bdf3c-ad5b-490f-b276-40554ad6f703) - {"connectorId":0,"meterValue":[{"timestamp":"2026-04-10T13:00:00.021Z","sampledValue":[{"value":"147989307.11595803","location":"Inlet","unit":"Wh","measurand":"Energy.Active.Import.Register","context":"Sample.Clock"}]}]}
These logs are taken from charger
Y2/S9 313873507001.
I hope I was able to provide you with clarification and answer your questions. Please let me know if you have any further question or need further support.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0481199-DC/Si-D/NL- [Y2 / S9 313873507001] Van Den Haak-data from AC MID meter CRM:00315003129
additional_info.body:
Dear Kanika,
I am reaching out following our conversation on MS Teams in regards of further updates on the topic. I am reporting here for traceability the latest information I provided you.
The feedback and statement in my last email within this ticket still stand:
According to OCPP 1.6, the charger can send MeterValues both for the “Outlet” location and for the “Inlet” location.
For the “Inlet” location, SichargeD sends the Energy.Active:Import.Register taken form the AC income meter for connectorId=0, hence the whole charger. This value is sent periodically according to the ClockAlignedDataInterval and it is included in the MetrValueAlignedData.
The SichargeD sends the AC income phases values only in case of AC charging on AC socket and only for “Outlet” location.
These points were already communicated to you and still stand. Last week we clarified further points with R&D. Here follows a breakdown of the information we received:
As specified in the SichargeD software manual, currently the only supported parameter taken form the AC income meter that Sicharge D supports in the MeterValuesAlignedData is the Energy.Active.Import.Register. This was an internal decision from R&D.
There is no FW/HW limitation from Sicharge D side to send the other parameters taken from the AC Income meter via OCPP.
The OCPP 1.6 standard specify that, for values taken from AC meter, the charger CAN share them as per total sum or per phase.
The internal decision of R&D was to send the Energy.Active.Import.Register only as sum value and not per phase.
In conclusion, if the End customer would like to retrieve further data from the AC income meter, this could be possible, as so far they are not transmitted due to internal FW implementation and not due to FW/HW constraints.
However, since this analysis did not identify a bug or an issue in the OCPP charger's implementation, but a feature not implemented, it is necessary for you to formally request it to our PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) as
Change Request
, as it is not a service topic anymore.
I hope I provided you with clarification to your questions. Please feel free to reach out if you need further support or to redirect you to the correct process to open a Change Request.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!
With kind regards,
